definition: A hypothetical particle. The QCD axion provides a compelling scheme to preserve CP symmetry in QCD, and the universe's cold dark matter may well consist of axions, which dedicated experiments search for.
locator: §89.1 Introduction
quote: The QCD axions is of particular interest because it provides a compelling scheme to preserve CP -symmetry in QCD. Moreover, the cold dark matter (CDM) of the Universe may well consist of axions and they are searched for in dedicated experiments with a realistic chance of discovery.
title: Axion

definition: The distance a neutrino beam travels from its source to the detector. K2K, the first long-baseline experiment, aimed a neutrino beam at Super-Kamiokande over a 250 km baseline.
locator: Section 14.6.3.3 'Long-baseline experiments' (the review also defines L as the source-to-detector distance in §14.4 and explains the long-baseline name in §14.6.3.1)
quote: K2K was the first long-baseline experiment and used a neutrino beam directed towards Super-Kamiokande with a 250 km baseline.
title: Baseline (long-baseline experiments)

definition: A detector that measures the energy and direction of particles by absorbing them in the detector material and registering the energy deposited in the resulting shower.
locator: §35.10.1 Calorimeters, Introduction, opening sentence
quote: A calorimeter measures the energy and direction of particles by absorption in the detector material and registration of the energy deposited in an (ideally) contained electromagnetic (EM) or hadronic shower.
title: Calorimeter

definition: The energy available in a collision. For example, the Intersecting Storage Rings' two proton beams collided with 62 GeV of centre-of-mass energy, equivalent to a 2000 GeV beam hitting a stationary target.
locator: Page body, second paragraph (Intersecting Storage Rings)
quote: Protons circulated in opposite directions and collided with a maximum centre-of-mass energy of 62 GeV. This is the equivalent of a 2000 GeV beam hitting a stationary target.
title: Centre-of-mass energy (√s)

definition: A neutrino interacts with an entire nucleus at once, rather than with the individual protons or neutrons inside it, as neutrinos typically do.
locator: Second paragraph of the article (CERN Courier, 22 September 2017)
quote: Typically, neutrinos interact with individual protons or neutrons inside a nucleus, but coherent elastic neutrino–nucleus scattering (CEνNS) occurs when a neutrino interacts with an entire nucleus.
title: Coherent elastic neutrino–nucleus scattering (CEνNS)

definition: Radiation emitted by a charged particle whose speed is greater than the local phase speed of light in the medium it travels through.
locator: §34.7 Cherenkov and transition radiation, opening paragraph
quote: A charged particle radiates if its speed is greater than the local phase speed of light (Cherenkov radiation)
title: Cherenkov light

definition: A confidence interval or limit is constructed so that, across many repeated experiments, at least the stated fraction of such intervals contain the true value. That fraction is the confidence level, as in a "95% CL" limit.
locator: Section 40.4.2 'Frequentist confidence intervals'
quote: The coverage probability refers to the fraction of intervals in such an ensemble that contain the true parameter value. Confidence intervals are constructed so as to have a coverage probability greater than or equal to a given confidence level, regardless of the true parameter's value.
title: Confidence level (CL)

definition: The laws of nature are not exactly the same for matter and for antimatter. If CP were an exact symmetry they would be the same, so CP violation is the difference.
locator: Opening paragraph of §13 (CP Violation in the Quark Sector)
quote: If CP were an exact symmetry, the laws of nature would be the same for matter and for antimatter.
title: CP violation

definition: A measure of the probability for a process to occur in a particle interaction. It is quoted in units such as the femtobarn (fb).
locator: FAQ answer to 'What is luminosity?'
quote: A femtobarn is a unit of cross-section, a measure of the probability for a process to occur in a particle interaction.
title: Cross-section

definition: The lowest energy a detector can register. PDG notes that most dark-matter searches lose sensitivity to light particles because their energy thresholds sit around a few hundred eV to a few keV.
locator: §27.6.2 Direct detection formalism, paragraph 'Scattering off bound electrons and absorption'
quote: most searches for DM-nucleus scattering rapidly lose sensitivity, due to energy thresholds around a few 100 eV - few keV.
title: Energy threshold

definition: How much data a rare-event search collects, quoted as detector mass multiplied by running time, in units such as tonne × year. DarkSide-20k, for example, is designed for 100 tonne × year over five years.
locator: Section 'Leading limits', paragraph on the GADMC two-step programme
quote: DarkSide-20k is designed to collect an exposure of 100 tonne × year in a period of five years (to be possibly extended to 200 tonne × year in 10 years)
title: Exposure

definition: The central region of a detector, chosen because its background rate from the surrounding materials is low. Defining it needs a three-dimensional position resolution.
locator: §27.6.3 Current and future direct detection technologies, first paragraph
quote: A 3D position resolution is required to define central detector regions (or fiducial volumes) with low background rates from surrounding materials
title: Fiducial volume and fiducial mass

definition: Instantaneous luminosity measures the number of potential collisions per unit area over a given time, an essential indicator of a collider's performance. Integrated luminosity measures the collected data size, in inverse femtobarns (fb⁻¹).
locator: FAQ answer to 'What is luminosity?' (the next sentence of the same answer defines integrated luminosity)
quote: which is the measure of the number of potential collisions per surface unit (or cross section) over a given period of time, is an essential indicator of an accelerator’s performance. Integrated luminosity is a measure of the collected data size and is measured in inverse femtobarns (fb -1 ).
title: Luminosity and integrated luminosity

definition: Shielding expressed as the thickness of water that would give the same shielding. For example, Baksan's Low Background Lab 3 is described as providing shielding equivalent to 4900 m of water.
locator: Section 'Current experiments' (Low Background Lab 3 at Baksan)
quote: a new experimental hall – Low Background Lab 3 on the figure above – located 3.67 km from the tunnel entrance (providing shielding equivalent of 4900 m of water)
title: Metres water equivalent (m.w.e.)

definition: Parameters of the neutrino mixing matrix. Neutrino oscillation searches show that it contains two large mixing angles and a third angle that is not exceedingly small.
locator: Opening paragraph of 'Neutrino Properties'
quote: However, the results of neutrino oscillation searches show that the mixing matrix contains two large mixing angles and a third angle that is not exceedingly small.
title: Neutrino mixing angles

definition: An active veto that rejects events occurring close in time to a crossing cosmic-ray muon, which removes the effect of the short-lived radioisotopes the muon produces.
locator: §36.6.5 Mitigation of backgrounds and active background discrimination, bullet 'Mitigation of cosmogenic background'
quote: Most of these radioisotopes are short-lived and their effect can be easily removed by an active veto based on the time correlation with a crossing muon.
title: Muon veto

definition: The ranking of the three neutrino masses m1, m2 and m3. Two orderings are possible: normal (m1 < m2 < m3) and inverted (m3 < m1 < m2).
locator: Section 14.7 (3ν paradigm), paragraph on the mass spectrum
quote: In this convention there are two non-equivalent orderings for the spectrum of neutrino masses: – Spectrum with Normal Ordering (NO) with m1 < m2 < m3 – Spectrum Inverted ordering (IO) with m3 < m1 < m2 .
title: Neutrino mass ordering (mass hierarchy)

definition: Neutrinos can change from one flavour into another as they travel long distances. The process is directly related to the neutrinos’ tiny mass.
locator: Page body, first paragraph (CERN Neutrinos to Gran Sasso)
quote: But it seems that neutrinos are the chameleons of the particle world: they can change from one flavour into another. This phenomenon, called “oscillation”, occurs as neutrinos travel long distances through matter. The process is directly related to the neutrinos’ tiny mass.
title: Neutrino oscillation

definition: A decay in which a nucleus (A, Z) becomes (A, Z + 2) and emits two electrons but no neutrinos. It is the most sensitive probe of whether neutrinos are Dirac or Majorana states.
locator: Section 14.9.2 'Dirac vs. Majorana: Neutrinoless Double-beta Decay' (the Majorana requirement and lepton-number violation are stated in the next lines)
quote: The most sensitive probe to whether neutrinos are Dirac or Majorana states is the neutrinoless double beta decay (0νββ): (A, Z) → (A, Z + 2) + e− + e− .
title: Neutrinoless double beta decay (0νββ)

definition: The recoil of a nucleus, as generated by interactions of neutrons, neutrinos or hypothetical WIMPs.
locator: §36.4 Large time-projection chambers for rare event detection, discussion of scintillation and ionisation yield
quote: For nuclear recoils as generated by interactions of neutrons, neutrinos or hypothetical WIMPs
title: Nuclear recoil

definition: Neutrinos emitted at an angle to the momentum of the parent mesons (the beam direction) form a narrow-band spectrum. Selecting those off-axis neutrinos is one way to generate such a spectrum.
locator: Opening paragraph of §33 (Neutrino Beam Lines at High-Energy Proton Synchrotrons)
quote: Another approach to generate a narrow-band neutrino spectrum is to select neutrinos that are emitted off-axis relative to the momentum of the parent mesons.
title: Off-axis angle

definition: The thickness of rock above an underground laboratory. At Gran Sasso, the 1400 metres of rock above the Laboratory reduce the cosmic-ray flux by one million times.
locator: Page body, paragraph on the rock thickness above the Laboratory
quote: The 1400 metre-rock thickness above the Laboratory represents a natural coverage that provides a cosmic ray flux reduction by one million times
title: Overburden

definition: A light sensor that multiplies an initial electron in repeated stages, typically about ten in series, until enough electrons reach the anode to deliver a signal to the external circuit.
locator: §35.2.1.1 Photomultiplier tubes, paragraph describing the dynode chain
quote: The multiplication process is repeated typically about 10 times in series to generate a sufficient number of electrons, which are collected at the anode for delivery to the external circuit.
title: Photomultiplier tube (PMT)

definition: A material that produces light when a charged particle passes through it.
locator: §35.3 Organic scintillators, opening sentence
quote: Organic scintillators produce light when transversed by a charged particle.
title: Scintillator

definition: The p-value of a result converted into an equivalent number of standard deviations (σ) of a Gaussian (bell-curve) distribution: the "N σ" quoted for a result.
locator: Section 40.3.2 (p-values and significance); the 5σ discovery convention is stated in the same paragraph block
quote: Often one converts the p-value into an effective significance Z, defined as an equivalent number of standard deviations of a Gaussian distributed random variable.
title: Significance (σ)

definition: A neutrino defined as having no Standard Model gauge interactions, so the Standard Model, which describes all known particle interactions, contains none.
locator: §14.1 Neutrinos in the Standard Model
quote: Sterile neutrinos are defined as having no SM gauge interactions, that is, they are singlets of the complete SM gauge group. Thus the SM, as the gauge theory able to describe all known particle interactions, contains no sterile neutrinos.
title: Sterile neutrino

definition: A circular accelerator in which particles are sped up each time they pass through accelerating cavities, while a growing magnetic field keeps them on an orbit of constant radius.
locator: Section 'The synchrotron' (adapted from CERN Courier vol. 1, September 1960, pp. 6-8)
quote: Every time the protons pass through one of the 16 accelerating cavities, their velocity is increased, while a growing magnetic field keeps their trajectory on an orbit of constant radius.
title: Synchrotron

definition: A detector in which a charged particle leaves a track of ionization electrons that drift in an electric field to a readout plane, which gives two coordinates. The arrival times of the electrons give the third.
locator: §35.6.4 Time-projection chambers, opening paragraph
quote: Charged particles produce tracks of ionization electrons that drift in a uniform electric field towards a position-sensitive amplification stage which provides a 2D projection of the particle trajectories. The third coordinate can be calculated from the arrival times of the drifted electrons.
title: Time projection chamber (TPC)

definition: Weakly interacting massive particles: one well-considered form of dark matter that matches astronomical measurements, and that would exist in our galaxy with defined numbers and velocities.
locator: Section 'Direct detection with liquid argon', second paragraph
quote: One well-considered form of dark matter that matches astronomical measurements is weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs), which would exist in our galaxy with defined numbers and velocities.
title: WIMP (weakly interacting massive particle)
